sample_unit: clinical scenarios (over 6,000; 7,000 physician annotations; 225,000 model responses)

links.outcome: LLM triage recommendation stability under clinically irrelevant text perturbations versus physicians
links.effect: LLMs recommended unnecessary care more often than physicians at baseline, and this tendency increased under perturbed inputs; LLMs varied under clinically irrelevant textual changes.
links.quote: First, LLMs are more likely than physicians to recommend unnecessary care at baseline, and this tendency increases under perturbed inputs.

links.outcome: Sensitivity of LLM triage recommendations to gender perturbations compared with physicians
links.effect: LLM recommendations were more sensitive to gender and tone perturbations than human physician recommendations.
links.quote: Further, we find that LLM recommendations are more sensitive to gender and tone perturbations than human recommendations.

links.outcome: Rate of unnecessary care (over-escalation) recommended by LLMs versus physicians
links.effect: LLMs were more likely than physicians to recommend unnecessary care at baseline, increasing under perturbed inputs.
links.quote: First, LLMs are more likely than physicians to recommend unnecessary care at baseline, and this tendency increases under perturbed inputs.

screen.reason: Empirical benchmark evaluating LLM sensitivity and robustness under clinical text, gender, and tone perturbations compared to physician expert annotations in a triage task.
